text:
erin: Quick help — opening an Azure support request to prep UK South for our GPU inference fleet. Need quota increases + PrivateLink endpoints to Storage & Log Analytics + extra NAT gateway public IPs. Who can file the support ticket?

devin: I can. Post the exact SKUs, quantities, subscription ID, and VNet/CIDR plan and Ill open the ticket. Also confirm whether we want central NAT or colocated NAT per subscription.

erin: Initial plan: 12 x Standard_NC6s_v3, target eventual capacity ~40 GPUs (across 2-3 node pools). Quotas to request: NC-series GPU family quota 0 -> 40, regional vCPU quota to cover SKUs, Public IPs for NAT gateway 1 -> 5, and network interface limit increase. Subscription: sub-0a1b2c3d. VNet plan: prod VNet = 10.40.0.0/20, nodepool subnet = 10.40.0.0/21 (Azure CNI, ~2k IPs), control plane /26, services /28. Reserve an extra /28 for PrivateEndpoints. PrivateLink targets: storage account (logs blob) + Log Analytics workspace.

devin: Got it. I'll open the ticket now. Quick question: prefer central NAT (infra subscription) with VNet peering + gateway transit, or create NAT in prod subscription? Central NAT makes egress auditing easier but requires gateway transit config.

erin: Prefer central NAT in infra subscription. We'll peer VNet-prod-uksouth -> VNet-infra-uksouth and enable gateway transit on infra side. UDRs in prod should point 0.0.0.0/0 -> NAT in infra subscription (no transitive routing).

raj: Heads up on route limits: Azure effective routes and prefixes per route table bump needed. Request increase to at least 500 effective routes for these VNets given UDRs + PrivateLink + peering. Also ask MSFT to confirm max peerings and gateway transit configuration. PrivateEndpoints will consume IPs in services subnet so account for that.

devin: Drafting justification for MSFT: "Production GPU inference fleet for Redwood Inference  low-latency regional serving; requires regional GPU quota and networking increases for VNet peering, NAT gateway public IPs, and PrivateLink endpoints to Storage and LogAnalytics." Requesting expedited review due to onboarding timeline next week.

infra-bot: azure-support: Support request created: AZURE-20260305-0001. Status: New. Portal link provided in ticket details.

sophie: Cost note: NAT gateway is a fixed charge; static public IPs cost extra. Rough estimate for 5 public IPs + NAT + 50TB egress/mo ~ $1.2k/mo. PrivateLink endpoints have per-hour + per-GB charges too. Tag finance.

devin: MSFT asked for subscription owner contact + expected sustained throughput. Erin, can you be the contact? They also want fallback region plan if quota takes time.

erin: I'll be the contact. Expected sustained: ~600 req/s across 40 GPUs after ramp. Fallback: UK West + Redwood hosted Dedicated on-demand if quota not approved in time.

devin: MSFT accepted the justification and asked for exact VNet names and peering pairs. I submitted: VNet-infra-uksouth (infra subscription) <-> VNet-prod-uksouth (prod subscription), gateway transit enabled on infra side. Also requested public IP quota and NC-series quota.

raj: Add NSG notes: ensure NSG allows PrivateEndpoint traffic; service endpoints alone won't cut it. Also document that PrivateEndpoint NICs use addresses from the services subnet. Reserve IPs accordingly.

erin: Good call. We'll reserve an extra /28 in services subnet specifically for PrivateEndpoints and management endpoints.

devin: Ticket updated: AZURE-20260305-0001 -> InReview. MSFT requested an IP usage CSV; attaching CIDR plan. They estimate 24-48h after approval to apply quota increases.

sophie: Tagging finance: @cloud-costs  expect spike in egress and static IP recurring costs if this goes live.

erin: Thanks all. Please ping this thread when ticket moves to Resolved so I can start cluster provisioning. :thumbsup:

devin: Will do. If anyone needs access to the support portal, DM me and Ill share the approval link.

Reference Terraform snippet (for nodepool subnet):
```
resource "azurerm_subnet" "gpu_nodes" {
  name                 = "snet-gpu-nodes"
  resource_group_name  = azurerm_resource_group.rg.name
  virtual_network_name = azurerm_virtual_network.vnet.name
  address_prefixes     = ["10.40.0.0/21"]
}
```
